question.text: A Power of Attorney (PoA) is executed by an Indian investor residing in London, UK. Which of the following correctly describes the requirements for the PoA to be valid?

answer.text: It must be executed on non-judicial stamp paper of the country where the grantor resides
It must be notarized by a local notary in the UK and apostilled under the Hague Convention

It may be executed on plain paper and attested by a designated Indian embassy official abroad or by a notary abroad, signed by the grantor on all pages, sent to India for the holder's signature, and stamped/notarized in India if required
It must be executed on Indian non-judicial stamp paper, which must be procured from India before execution

explanation.text: The Logic: For a PoA executed abroad by an Indian investor, the prescribed procedure (per NISM Series X-A) is: the PoA may be typed on plain paper, attested by a designated Indian embassy official abroad OR by a notary abroad, signed by the grantor on all pages, then sent to India for the holder's signature and stamped/notarized in India if required. This is the full set of requirements stated by the source. The Trap: The original keyed option (embassy/consulate attestation only) was too narrow because the source also permits notary-abroad attestation and adds further India-side steps. The apostille option is incorrect because the source does not specify apostille under the Hague Convention. Stamp-paper-abroad options are wrong because plain paper is permitted when executed outside India. Note: Source: NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1), June 2025, pp. 306-307. The correct option has been rewritten to match the full procedure listed on p. 307 (plain paper, embassy-official OR notary-abroad attestation, signature on all pages, holder signature in India, stamp/notarize in India if required) to remove ambiguity.
